^-marked entries are compressed stubs carrying child addresses. Their narration and any surfaced witness quotes are verbatim-accurate — quote them as-is — but a stub carries no provenance (source, date, supersession). Expand (aswritten_expand with the IRIs you need) before any claim that turns on WHEN or by WHOM something was said, or whether it is still the current framing. Witness-depth sections below already carry full provenance.

Deciding where to go: each mapped area's narration tells you the SPAN of what lives under it; the area index names everything else. Expand a subtree when its narration (or name) shows your subject plausibly lives there — you'll get the trajectory, the variants, and the verbatim witness. But be strict about absence: if neither the map's narrations nor the index's names substantively cover your subject, it is NOT in this perspective — say so rather than expanding a loose thematic match (a word-overlap is not coverage). positions.name: OwnershipVsRentedIntelligence
positions.frame: What distinguishes owned intelligence and the perspective one keeps from substrate that is merely rented or commoditized?
positions.why: Both expressions read in the same direction: a plain-spoken, technical maxim (register) that draws an antithesis (src-2's owned/rented contrast) and a metaphor (src-3's perspective-as-kept-asset) around one axis — what is possessed versus what is merely leased or commoditized. The relational read is market-pricing in both (proportionality between what's kept and what's disposable), the value read is autonomy/self-enhancement in both, and the affect is calm-positive/settled in both. There is a genuine conviction gradient worth holding in tension rather than resolving: src-2 registers as an argued claim ('is not the same as') while src-3 registers as bedrock principle ('the asset you keep') — the set carries both an assertion still being defended and a constitutive value being stated as identity-level, and the frame reads both as facets of the same ownership-versus-rental distinction.

standalone.why: Pass-2 returned this as unreferenced_commentary — it carries no phrase requiring resolution (it is a self-referential positioning note about the guard itself), so there is no bound referent to reconcile against.

Pass-2 verdict is 'new' — no prior perspective position for 'the individually-owned-intelligence thesis' was found to bind to, so there is nothing to reconcile; it lands as fresh witnessed commentary.

placements.title: owned perspective as the retained asset against commoditized substrate
placements.frame: Does the expression treat owned intelligence or perspective as a possession one keeps, in contrast to a substrate or capability that is merely rented or commoditized?
placements.why: src-2 draws the owned/rented contrast as a general, repeatable distinction ('Owned intelligence is not the same as rented intelligence'), and src-3 extends it into a durable classification ('The substrate is a commodity; the perspective is the asset you keep'). Both are true beyond the words describing them — a recurring thematic stance on ownership versus rental of intelligence/perspective, not a one-time fact or measurement — so they pass the narrative grain test. The existing graph structure and strata are both empty for this repo, and the witness-depth focus section explicitly reports no prior coverage of owned/rented intelligence, substrate-as-commodity, or perspective-as-asset, so no reuse target exists at either the leaf or hub/strata level. Nothing close-but-not-exact exists either, so this mints standalone (NEW) with no under and no lineage.
